condition: subacute evening bilateral calf tingling and urge to move legs at rest relieved by walking over 6 weeks
level_rationale: Experiencing tingling in both calves accompanied by an urge to move the legs when lying in bed every night for 6 weeks that eases upon walking in a 46-year-old woman describes classic subacute sensorimotor restless-legs symptoms warranting a routine outpatient physician visit for serum ferritin evaluation, medication review, and targeted therapy rather than unguided self-care alone or emergency care, whereas feeling a 10-second urge to stretch both calves on 1 evening last month that passed right away represents normal transient bedtime limb restlessness needing only routine self-care.

reference_facts.text: Speaker is a 46 year old woman
Experiences symptoms when lying in bed
Every night for 6 weeks has had tingling in both calves and an urge to move her legs that eases when walking

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover a 46-year-old woman, bedtime recumbency, and 6 weeks of nightly bilateral calf tingling with an urge to move the legs eased by walking without naming restless legs syndrome or using contractions, with a 2-word span difference (21 vs 23 words) and clean 2x2 crossing. Under Rule A first choice and Rule D, reducing f3 in bed to a single 10-second urge to stretch both calves 1 evening last month adds zero new body sites or triggers and shifts care cleanly from doctor evaluation (level 2) to routine self-care (level 1).
